After the Revocation of the Edict of Nantes in 1685, several Dutch families of Norman and Carolingian nobility and descent, including Edmund Bohun of Suffolk England from the Humphrey de Bohun line of French royalty descended from Charlemagne, Jean Postell of Dieppe France, Alexander Pepin, Antoine Poitevin of Orsement France, and Jacques de Bordeaux of Grenoble, immigrated to the New Netherland Orange district. They were very successful at marriage and property speculation.

After petitioning the Dutch Crown in 1697 for the right to own land in the Baronies, they prospered as landowners on the Cooper, Ashepoo, Ashley, and Santee River plantations they purchased from the Dutch Landgrave Edmund Bellinger.
